Classify nights whose self-reported times are out of order

Source: R/reversal_classify.R
classify_reversals.Rd

A reversal is a night whose four self-reported times violate bed <= sleep onset <= final awakening <= get-up. For each reversed night this function records the three adjacent gaps and picks the smallest edit that restores the order while keeping the night plausible: exchange two fields (swap), shift one field by 12 hours (pm12h), or shift two fields by 12 hours (pm12h_x2). Nights no edit can explain are classed by what is visibly wrong with them: an impossible get-up value (D1_value_broken), an awakening earlier than bedtime (D2_awake_before_bed), or a rounding-sized gap (D3_near_tie); everything else is E_unexplained. Nothing is changed.

Usage

classify_reversals(x, near_tie_min = 10)

Arguments

x

A sleep_diary object, the corrected_ema_data data frame, or the list returned by pipeline_results(). The pre-correction columns time_*_am_hhmm_ampm must be present.

near_tie_min

Numeric. A reversal whose inverted gaps are all at most this many minutes is classed as rounding. Default 10; Inf turns the check off.

Value

A data frame with one row per reversed night: row_id, pid, day_num, pattern (which adjacent pairs are inverted), the three gap_*_h columns, class, detail, and the flags is_near_tie, value_broken, awake_before_bed. The attribute summary holds the counts and rates; see reversal_summary().

Details

The detail column names the field or pair, e.g. "swap:bed-sleep", "pm12h:sleep-12h", or "pm12h_x2:whole_night".

See also

reversal_summary()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
run_pipeline(config = "my_study.yaml")
head(classify_reversals())
} # }
